children.value: This chapter relates the trial-locked heart rate to the outcome types, to Nexus surprise and state uncertainty, to the model-free prediction error and to the instruction condition. The session-level heart rate and heart-rate variability are related to the general factor (

) and STICSA trait. Heart rate is set against the pupil, and the feedback response is tested as a predictor of the next placement and gaze. The analyses use the predictors and model forms of the pupil analyses (
Pupil and the Latent Signals of Three Models
), so the two signals can be compared directly. The measures are described in
Run 23_11. Scripts (analysis repository) and pipeline steps:
session level, heart rate and pupil, time lag

Correction: Benjamini-Hochberg. A family is the set of tests that answer one question about one heart-rate measure. Outcome-type contrasts and model signals (Nexus surprise and state uncertainty) are separate questions, the three heart-rate measures are separate measures, and the general factor and STICSA trait are corrected separately. The model-free prediction error is in the models as a control and is reported without correction. Each section names its families; all are defined in

The data set contains 93 participants (None 36, Partial 35, Full 22) and 15,688 trials; 92 participants have questionnaire scores. Trials after a rating or break screen are left out, as in the pupil analysis.
